requestedActions.title: Read titles of work packages the connected person can access, including pagination
Authorize the connected OpenProject person via developer-owned OAuth on their own instance

guide.summary: OpenProject documents developer-owned OAuth2 for its API, with authorization code flow acting as the connected person. Reading work package titles is limited to what that person can see, and the documented default OAuth scope is api_v3.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: Authorization code flow acts as the connected user with a bearer token
findings.detail: OpenProject's OAuth2 server exposes auth and token URLs on the instance; the client obtains a code via the authorize URL and exchanges it at the token endpoint for a Bearer access token used to call the API on behalf of the current user. Tokens expire after two hours by default and a refresh token is issued.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer-owned OpenProject instance with a connected person acting as themselves

evidence.quote: Authorization code flow example
With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.
Please note that your Bearer token will expire after two hours (default) and you will have to click on “Request Token” again. Otherwise your API request will return an error

findings.title: Register an OAuth application on each customer instance with redirect URL and client credentials
findings.detail: An administrator must create an OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications, define a redirect URL, choose Confidential if applicable, and record the Client ID and secret. Each customer instance needs its own registration because the instance base URL is user input.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer organization or workspace that connects

findings.title: Default api_v3 scope is the standard API scope for OAuth applications
findings.detail: If no scope is checked on the OAuth application, api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API. Read access to work packages is then governed by each person's own permissions, not by a separate OAuth scope.
findings.appliesWhen: Default or explicitly selected api_v3 scope on the customer OAuth application

findings.title: Work package listing returns only work packages the connected person can see
findings.detail: The work package collection endpoint returns accessible work packages; the visible scope factors permissions into the fetch, so an empty collection is returned when the user lacks permission. Pagination uses offset and pageSize parameters, and the default filter applies unless an empty filters array is sent.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading accessible work package titles through the list endpoint

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
a visible scope which factors the permissions into the SQL fetching the records. That way, an empty collection is returned if the user lacks permission. If an explicit 403 needs
pageSize integer optional query

findings.title: Confirm the connected person can view work packages in target projects
findings.detail: Accessible work package visibility depends on the person's project roles, which are separate from the OAuth scope. Collection responses document offset-based and cursor-based pagination only where available, so response links must be checked during testing.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer testing with representative account access

steps.title: Register developer-owned OAuth application on the customer instance
steps.detail: An administrator on the customer's OpenProject instance creates an OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications. Define a redirect URL provided by the developer's client, leave the default api_v3 scope, and choose Confidential only if the client runs on a server. Record the Client ID and Client secret. Each instance needs its own registration; the instance base URL is a user input.
steps.doneWhen: The OAuth application exists on the instance and its Client ID, client secret and redirect URL are recorded for the developer's client.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Add a new authentication application for OAuth
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer-provided full HTTPS origin of their OpenProject instance
CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: from the OAuth application created in the instance admin UI
REDIRECT_URI: must match the developer client's configured redirect URL

steps.title: Obtain authorization code through the consent redirect
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser as the connected person. The person approves access and is redirected to the redirect URI with a code parameter. Verify the callback contains a code value before exchanging it. This step is a manual consent action; no request is executed by the agent.
steps.doneWhen: The browser callback URL contains a code query parameter for the connected person.

evidence.quote: Request authorization code Request an authorization code. Please adopt the following URL replacing:

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
In this example we skip that server side implementation and just copy the value of the code parameter from the URL that you see in your browser.

fields: CLIENT_ID: from the registered OAuth application
REDIRECT_URI: the configured redirect URL
scope: api_v3 is the documented default scope
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for bearer access token
steps.detail: Exchange the code at the token endpoint using the documented form fields. The response contains access_token and refresh_token; the access token expires after two hours by default. This is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.

evidence.quote: $ curl --request POST \
--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

fields: AUTH_CODE: value of the code parameter from the callback URL
CLIENT_SECRET: from the OAuth application registration
grant_type: documented constant authorization_code
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Read first page of accessible work package titles
steps.detail: List work packages visible to the connected person using the documented collection endpoint with pagination parameters. Titles are in each element's subject property under _embedded.elements. Send an empty filters array so the default status filter is not applied.
steps.doneWhen: The response is a Collection with _embedded.elements entries each carrying a subject string, and _links.nextByOffset is present when more pages exist. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
can issue further requests to retrieve the remaining elements. There are two ways to access the result pages of a paginated collection:
Example: 25 filters string

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: bearer token from the token exchange step
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
filters=%5B%5D: empty array to disable the default status filter

steps.title: Read next page of work package titles using offset
steps.detail: Repeat the list request with offset incremented, preserving pageSize and filters, until the collection's total is reached. Stop when count plus offset-derived position covers total. Titles are read from each element's subject.
steps.doneWhen: Successive offset pages cover all elements up to the reported total.

evidence.quote: offset The page number that is requested from paginated collection Integer when offset based available
nextByOffset Link to retrieve the following page of elements (offset based) when offset based available
offset integer optional query

fields: offset: next page number from the prior response's offset/total metadata
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
Access token: backend OAuth exchange for the test account; keep it out of this guide

steps.title: Continue paginating accessible work package listing
steps.detail: After page one, repeat the same collection request with offset incremented by 1 (2, 3, and so on) while keeping pageSize=25 and filters=[]. Alternatively follow the returned nextByOffset link unchanged. Read subject from each element in _embedded.elements. Stop only when the cumulative count of elements read equals the collection total property. Boundary check: confirm the outgoing requests are GET calls to the work packages collection only, with no modify or delete calls.
steps.doneWhen: All pages through total are read and every element subject has been collected. Boundary check: the request log shows only GET requests to /api/v3/work_packages and no update or delete operations.

evidence.quote: offset The page number that is requested from paginated collection Integer when offset based available
nextByOffset Link to retrieve the following page of elements (offset based) when offset based available
total The total amount of elements available in the collection Integer always

pageSize: 25, same as page one
